_readme: COPY THIS TO presets.json TO USE IT. The file is read from the extension
folder, which every browser profile in an AdsPower-style fleet shares — so
one copy configures all of them.
IT IS AUTHORITATIVE AND RE-APPLIED ON EVERY LAUNCH. Settings changed by hand
in a profile last until that profile next starts. That is the point: a rate
cap changed here has to land everywhere, including on the profile somebody
tweaked last week.
If it does not parse, or names a platform this build does not know, NOTHING
is applied and every profile keeps the settings it already had. Check the
Presets tab — it says so there.
Produce a real one with Presets -> Save -> Export rather than writing it by
hand; that guarantees the field names match the build you are running.
`schedule` is each day's windows as [from, to], on this profile's OWN
clock — so a fleet on per-profile timezones keeps each account on local
hours. An end EARLIER than its start runs into the next day: Friday's
22:00-02:00 below is Friday night. Outside these hours the account is
silent: no sweep, no automatic replies, no follow-ups. A week that does
not parse fails CLOSED and the whole file is refused, because the
alternative is fifty real accounts running around the clock.
`accounts` maps a signed-in handle to a preset name, which is how ONE file
serves a fleet running different characters: every profile reads the same
bytes and picks its own row once it knows which account it is. Unrecognised
handles get `default`, so a newly added account starts working rather than
sitting unconfigured.
